messages:
mira: quick heads-up — after the RBAC refactor deployed last night we're seeing embeddings requests accepted with chat-only tokens on /v1/embeddings

samir: ugh. can you paste a minimal log or repro?

mira: logs show incoming request to /v1/embeddings model=embed-large, auth scope header indicates scopes=["chat:generate"] but the request returned 200 and produced an embedding. snippet: 

    Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx
    X-Route: /v1/embeddings
    request.body: {"input":"test"}

alex: ops-bot noted the RBAC policy key rename in the refactor (scope_key -> surface_type) — could be a mismatch between policy tags and the runtime enforcement check.

jen: timeline: deploy finished 02:12 UTC, first anomalous hit at 02:18 UTC, spike ~02:20-02:45. ops-bot:deploy posted success message.

ops-bot: deploy "rbac/refactor/surface-type" completed by samir at 2026-02-18T02:12:03Z :white_check_mark:

samir: repro steps I used: 1) create token with only chat:generate 2) call embeddings endpoint with model embed-large 3) observe 200 + embedding vector. Happened locally against staging too when we applied same policies.

alex: likely cause hypothesis: enforcement layer still reads the old policy attribute name (scope_key) for per-route allowlists. During refactor we updated policy documents to use surface_type, but the enforcement shim has a fallback that treats unknown keys as permissive (intentional to avoid outages) — that fallback is the bug now.

mira: confirmed: policy DB entries have surface_type=\"embeddings\" for the route, but enforcement code looked up scope_key and got null -> allowed.

jen: immediate mitigations?

samir: temp fix options: 1) rollback refactor (fast but roll-back cost) 2) patch enforcement to fail-closed when policy key absent (safer but needs careful testing) 3) populate legacy scope_key via backfill script from surface_type (quickest stopgap).

alex: I'd prefer backfill + patch: backfill policy records in DB to set scope_key=surface_type for all per-route entries, then deploy enforcement change to warn but still allow for N hours before fail-closed. That minimizes customer impact.

mira: agree. also need to rotate any tokens we think leaked broader perms. We should identify tokens used during window 02:18-02:45 via audit logs.

jen: action items: 
- samir: run DB backfill with dry-run and then commit (ETA 2h)
- alex: open PR for enforcement shim to log a warning when key mismatch and add feature flag for fail-closed (ETA 3h)
- mira: compile list of tokens from audit logs and propose rotation list (ETA 1.5h)
- jen: create incident ticket + customer comms draft (JIRA INF-1227)

samir: note — we should check KMS-wrapped key metadata too. if we backfilled policy tags but KMS key tags are out of sync the authz check that cross-references KMS metadata could also slip.

alex: good call. mira, can you grep audit logs for any KMS rewrap events around deploy time? specifically look for keytag writes at 02:10-02:30.

mira: on it — found two rewraps at 02:09 and 02:11 for customer service keys. none coincident with the anomalous tokens but I'll attach logs to the ticket.

jen: customer impact? low so far but needs priority: embeddings customers with per-route allowlists could have seen unintended access if they used chat-only tokens. recommend proactive outreach if we rotate tokens.

ops-bot: created incident INF-1227: "RBAC key-name refactor -> permissive fallback for per-route allowlist" assigned to eng-security, priority=P1

samir: starting backfill dry-run now. will post results in this thread.

mira: thanks — please add any token findings to INF-1227. I'll prepare recommended rotation script and a snippet to invalidate session tokens in the window.

alex: long-term: add unit tests asserting enforcement reads both legacy and new keys and fail-closed on unknown attributes. also consider a migration tool that validates no live discrepancy post-deploy.

jen: cool. keep thread updated. :lock:
